comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor locations and clearance dimensions are required to demonstrate that buildings maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No such documentation is present on the site plan.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8, particularly Building 1 and Building 8 (closest to overhead electric lines on western and southern boundaries)
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) confirms overhead electric utility lines (O.H.U.L.) with utility poles exist along Valley View Road (western boundary) and southern property boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1-8 with Building 1 dimensioned at 26.1' and Building 8 at 26.6' from the western property line. Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) references existing OHE lines. However, NO building elevation sheets are provided in the 39-sheet set. NO dimension annotations show horizontal clearances from buildings to the outside conductor of overhead lines. NO surveyed conductor elevations are shown on any drawings.
reasoning: While buildings are set back approximately 26+ feet from the property line, the requirement is to maintain a 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of overhead electric conductors. Without surveyed conductor elevation data, clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to building faces, and no building elevation drawings showing the vertical relationship, it is impossible to verify that the minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. The code requires clearance measured from the outside conductor (which may be offset several feet from the pole center on multi-conductor installations), not from the pole or property line. Applicant has acknowledged responsibility for maintaining clearances (Sheet 3, Block 8), but has not provided the necessary documentation to demonstrate compliance.

comment: Plan documentation required: (1) identification of existing conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on overhead lines; (2) dimension annotations showing minimum 15-foot radial clearance from buildings and other customer facilities to the outside conductor of distribution primary and neutral conductors; (3) clarification of whether existing lines are distribution or transmission voltage.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 in relation to distribution primary and neutral conductors on western and southern boundaries
observation: Sheets 4, 9, and 21 confirm existing overhead electric (O.H.U.L.) facilities adjacent to the property. However, the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not labeled or identified on any plans. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies specifically to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No dimension annotations show radial clearances from any building or customer facility to these conductors. No plan notes identify whether the existing lines are distribution (voltage <60kV) or transmission (voltage ≥60kV), and no conductor types are labeled.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (including buildings) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of distribution primary and neutral conductors. Without identification of conductor types and without dimension annotations showing radial clearances from buildings to the conductors, compliance cannot be verified. The 15-foot clearance measurement requires identification of which conductors are primary/neutral vs. secondary, and this distinction is absent from the plans.

comment: Building elevation or section exhibits are required showing all projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) with dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of projections, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs) for Buildings 1-8
observation: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows buildings 1-8 with footprints and general layout, but no section views or elevation drawings depicting building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead electric conductors. No surveyed conductor elevations are provided. Building architectural details or elevations showing projection dimensions are not included in the 39-sheet set.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires building projections to maintain both (1) 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors. Without section views or elevation drawings showing the vertical and horizontal relationships between building projections and the overhead conductors, and without surveyed conductor elevation data, compliance with these requirements cannot be verified. Buildings can only be shown in plan view without cross-sections showing their height relative to conductor height.

comment: Surveyed elevations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations from the outside conductor to building faces are required, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from electric facilities in the adjacent Valley View Road right-of-way.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, 8 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead utility lines and utility poles along Valley View Road (western boundary). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1, 2, and 8 positioned near the western property line adjacent to Valley View Road ROW. Building 1 is dimensioned at 26.1' from the western property line; Building 8 at 26.6'. However, NO surveyed conductor elevation data is shown, NO dimension annotations show clearances from buildings to the outside conductor, and NO section views demonstrate that permanent 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from electric facilities in the adjacent ROW.
reasoning: No surveyed elevation data or clearance dimensions provided showing that buildings adjacent to Valley View Road maintain required permanent clearances from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities in ROW. Proximity survey data by registered surveyor is needed.

comment: Building elevation sheets prepared by the architect/engineer are required, showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations with clearance dimension annotations from the conductor to building faces, roofs, parapets, and all projections, for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: All buildings proposed within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
observation: The 39-sheet site plan set does not include any building elevation sheets. Sheet 9 shows building footprints and FFEs but is a plan view only. The README index lists sheets 1-39 with the following titles: Sheets 1-11 are general plans; Sheets 12-20 are utility and drainage plans; Sheets 21-39 are details and landscape plans. NO sheets titled 'Building Elevations,' 'Building Elevation Sheets,' or similar are listed. Consequently, surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not present on any elevation sheets.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors to be included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met. The absence of building elevation sheets constitutes a failure to provide the required documentation. The code requirement is specific: 'Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors not included on building elevation sheets to demonstrate required clearances are met' is identified as a deficiency.

comment: Provide section view exhibits (with title callouts such as Section A-A, B-B) on site plan or separate detail sheets showing dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of each building and all building projections, clearly labeling clearances in feet and inches.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric lines
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings in plan view only with no section line callouts (A-A, B-B, etc.) that would reference section views showing clearances. Sheet 22 shows standard construction details for curbs, sidewalks, and driveways but contains no section views specifically showing clearances from outer electric conductor to building edges. Sheets 38-39 show wall construction details and sections but not clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to wall faces. Examined sheets do not include section or plan view exhibits with dimension lines originating at the outer electric conductor and extending to building edges or wall faces.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'Section and plan view exhibits [that] show dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and building projections for clearance verification.' This is a specific documentation requirement. The absence of any section views with dimension lines from the outer conductor to building edges or wall faces constitutes non-compliance. The requirement applies when buildings or structures are proposed within potential clearance distance, which is the case here.

comment: Provide section views of retaining walls showing the surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clearance dimensions (measured horizontally) from the outside conductor location to the near face of the retaining wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls, particularly along southern property boundary where OHE line is located
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows retaining walls labeled 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall' along the southern boundary and other site perimeter locations. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) shows an overhead electric line (O.H.U.L.) running along the southern property boundary. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans) provide wall construction sections showing max 14-foot height, reinforcement details, and structural dimensions, but contain NO sections showing clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor to the wall face or top. Wall plan sheets show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure calculations, not clearances to adjacent overhead lines.
reasoning: The requirement under UCM § 1.10.3 is to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. Retaining walls up to 14 feet tall are proposed along the southern boundary where overhead electric lines are present. Without section views showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the distance (measured horizontally at ground level) from the conductor to the wall face, compliance cannot be verified. The wall height is known (up to 14 feet from foundation), but the conductor height and horizontal distance from the conductor to the wall are not documented.

comment: Provide section view exhibits of each retaining wall showing the surveyed outside conductor location with dimension lines to the outermost edge (top/face) of the wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the conductor to the wall.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric facilities on southern and eastern boundaries
observation: Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans and Wall Details) contain section views of retaining walls showing structural reinforcement, backfill requirements, footing details, and maximum heights (14 feet). However, these section views show only internal wall construction and soil pressure relationships. NO section views include dimension lines showing clearance from an outer electric conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of the retaining wall. Sheet 9 shows OHE line along southern boundary, but Sheets 38-39 do not cross-reference or show the conductor on their wall sections.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifically requires 'Retaining walls lack section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall for clearance verification' to be addressed. This is an explicit documentation requirement. The wall construction sections present on Sheets 38-39 do not show the overhead conductor location or clearance dimensions from the conductor to the wall. The requirement is for section exhibits that include both the wall profile AND the conductor location with a dimensioned clearance.

comment: Provide grading profile sections for proposed driveways showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations at the low point and dimension annotations verifying minimum 16-foot or 18-foot vertical clearance (depending on truck traffic designation) from the lowest point of all overhead conductors and attached equipment to the finished driveway surface.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways crossing or passing under or adjacent to overhead electric facilities
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows driveways marked 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway' on the western and internal portions of the site. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows existing and proposed contours with driveway grades and spot elevations, but contains NO profile sections showing the vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached telecommunications lines) to the driveway surface. Sheet 22 shows standard driveway construction details (thickness, reinforcement, grades) but NO sections showing vertical clearance to overhead lines. The FFE elevations of buildings are provided (ranging from 683' to 687.5' NAVD 88), but overhead conductor elevations are not given.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires driveways to maintain minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (for parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot vertical clearance (for areas with truck traffic) from the lowest point of overhead electric facilities including telecommunications attachments. This requires (1) surveyed conductor height data, (2) profile or section views showing clearance calculations, and (3) mid-span clearance verification if the clearance appears marginal. None of these are provided. Applicant has not verified mid-span clearances with registered surveyor data, and no vertical clearance dimensions are shown on grading or profile sheets.

comment: Provide section views of parking areas with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, or 18 feet for areas with truck traffic) from lowest point of conductors to finished parking surface. Add note to site plan specifying clearance requirement and designation of parking areas (truck vs. non-truck traffic).
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas beneath overhead electric lines
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces for a total of 88 spaces (per site plan data table). The parking layout is shown on the plan view, but NO section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to the parking surface. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows parking pad elevations and site topography but does not provide surveyed conductor heights or clearance verification. No note on site plan indicates the vertical clearance requirement or that parking must maintain minimum clearance from overhead lines.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires parking areas to maintain minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic). Without surveyed conductor elevations and section views showing the vertical relationship between parking pads and conductors, compliance cannot be verified. Additionally, a site plan note is required indicating the clearance requirement. No such note is present on Sheets 9 or 11.

comment: All clearance annotations must be revised to show dimension lines originating at the surveyed outside conductor location (not pole center), with clear identification of which conductor is being measured from, and dimension values showing clearances in feet and inches from the conductor to site features.
applicableAreas: All proposed site features and infrastructure
observation: Complete review of Sheets 9 (Site Plan), 11 (Grading Plan), and 21 (Electrical Plan) reveals NO dimension annotations showing clearances from buildings, structures, driveways, walls, or other site features to overhead electric lines. The only distances shown are from property lines and internal site features to each other. Sheet 4 shows the existing utility poles with symbols but no dimension annotations from the poles. No dimension lines on any sheet are shown extending from an identified 'outside conductor' location to site features. Applicant has not labeled the location of outside conductors or the measurement reference point for any clearance annotations.
reasoning: All clearance dimensions (or lack thereof) must be measured from the outside conductor, not from pole center or pole structure. No clearance dimensions are provided on the plans at all, and no plans identify the location of the outside conductor for measurement purposes.

comment: Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing clearance distance from proposed sidewalk alignment to existing power poles at each end of the property along Valley View Road right-of-way frontage. Confirm sidewalk clearance from pole locations, particularly at northwest and southwest property corners.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks along Valley View Road at property limits
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows utility poles along Valley View Road adjacent to the property. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows a proposed '5' Concrete Sidewalk' labeled 'Construct 5' Concrete Sidewalk' in the sidewalk easement area along the western property boundary adjacent to Valley View Road. However, Sheet 9 provides NO dimension annotations showing the alignment of the proposed sidewalk relative to the existing utility poles. The sidewalk alignment appears to follow the property line, but the exact horizontal distance from poles is not dimensioned. Sheet 22 shows standard sidewalk construction details but contains no site-specific dimension relating the sidewalk to pole locations.
reasoning: The requirement under Reviewer Convention is that sidewalks must be 'cleared from existing power poles at each end of property along right-of-way.' This implies that the sidewalk should not conflict with or be immediately adjacent to pole locations at property corners. Without dimension annotations showing the distance from the proposed sidewalk to existing pole locations at the northwest and southwest property corners where the property meets Valley View Road, compliance cannot be verified. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted an 'AT&T Pole' at the northwest corner, suggesting a utility pole exists at or near that location.

comment: Provide comprehensive easement exhibit on site plan showing all recorded easements (Greenbelt Access, City Drainage, 5' Electric Easements ×2, 7.5' Public Utility Easement, and any others per county records) with accurate boundary dimensions. Provide registered surveyor proximity survey confirming: (1) no customer facilities are located under or over overhead distribution lines (absolute prohibition); (2) all facilities within electric easement boundaries maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor; (3) all facilities comply with easement use restrictions.
applicableAreas: All proposed customer facilities, building structures, and site features relative to existing electric easements and overhead distribution facilities
observation: Facts.md identifies two perpetual easements with NO development permitted: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres) in NE interior—explicitly marked as 'strict no-build zone'; (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres) in NE corner with unlimited City access rights. Both are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (facts.md: 'NOT depicted on the submitted site plan and NOT in the COA GIS easement layer'). Additionally, a 5' Electric Easement (×2) and 7.5' Public Utility Easement are plat-dedicated per facts.md but locations relative to proposed improvements are not verified on site plans. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show all easements, but facts.md notes these are not shown. Sheet 9 shows the general site layout and street easements, but does not clearly depict all recorded electric easement boundaries or verify that proposed features maintain adequate clearance from easement areas.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: 'customer facilities proposed to be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities' is prohibited 'regardless of clearance distances.' Additionally, items within electric easements must maintain minimum 7.5-foot clearance from the outside conductor. The facts.md documentation reveals that critical easements (Greenbelt, Drainage, Electric, PUE) are either not depicted or not verified on the site plan. Without accurate easement boundaries shown on plans, applicant cannot demonstrate that (1) no facilities are placed under/over overhead distribution lines in violation of the absolute prohibition, or (2) items within easements maintain required 7.5-foot clearances. A proximity survey by registered surveyor is required to confirm easement boundaries and facility compliance.

comment: Provide registered surveyor field survey data documenting: (1) surveyed elevations of overhead electric conductors at mid-span locations above buildings, driveways, and parking areas; (2) calculated vertical clearances from the lowest point of conductors (including attachments) to the highest points of buildings, roof projections, driveways, and parking surfaces, demonstrating compliance with minimum clearance thresholds (7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground for buildings, 16-18 feet for driveways/parking, others as applicable); (3) marked survey points and elevation measurements with registered surveyor certification.
applicableAreas: All proposed driveways, parking areas, buildings, and site features with potential vertical clearance concerns from overhead electric lines
observation: Overhead electric lines (O.H.U.L.) are shown on existing survey (Sheet 4) and electrical plan (Sheet 21) but NO surveyed conductor elevation data is provided anywhere on the 39-sheet site plan set. Buildings have FFEs ranging from 683' to 687.5' (Sheet 9, 11), but overhead conductor heights are not documented. Driveways and parking pads have grading elevations shown (Sheet 11), but no profile sections with surveyed mid-span clearance data verify vertical clearances meet requirements. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 noted that buildings are approximately 26-30 feet horizontally from overhead lines on the western boundary—this distance is close enough that vertical clearance verification (mid-span clearance) should be provided per UCM § 1.10.3 guidance for situations where 'clearance appears marginal or insufficient.' No registered surveyor data confirming mid-span clearance is provided.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 'survey by registered surveyor showing pole locations and mid-span clearances not provided when existing overhead facilities may not meet minimum vertical clearance requirements.' The grouping guidance states that when vertical clearance 'appears marginal or insufficient based on site plan data,' registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required. The site plan does not provide surveyed conductor elevations, making it impossible to calculate vertical clearances from building FFEs and driveway grades to conductor height. Furthermore, the presence of structures within approximately 26-30 feet horizontally of overhead lines, combined with the absence of conducted elevator data, suggests that clearance verification is required but not provided. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide surveyor data for mid-span clearances.

comment: Provide detailed photometric plan or lighting layout showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances, OR; (3) relocation notes if fixtures cannot meet clearance requirements. Include note on site plan indicating clearance requirement for lighting.
applicableAreas: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site
observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan, Block 2) includes a 'Lighting Note' requiring all exterior lighting to be 'full cut-off and fully shielded in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5' and providing 'Figure 34: Examples of Fully-Shielded Light Fixtures.' This addresses design standards for light shielding but does NOT address clearances from overhead electric lines. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the site layout with various landscape elements but does not include dimension annotations showing horizontal or vertical clearances from proposed light fixtures to overhead electric lines. No site plan contains a photometric plan or detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations with clearance dimensions.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires decorative lighting proposed under existing overhead electric lines to meet clearance requirements (7.5-foot sky-to-ground horizontal, 15-foot radial) or be relocated. The site plan shows a general requirement for 'full cut-off' lighting compliance but does not identify where exterior lighting fixtures will be located or provide clearance verification from overhead conductors. Without a detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations and without clearance dimensions from conductors, compliance cannot be verified. If lighting is proposed beneath or within 15 feet of overhead conductors, relocation or clearance documentation is required.

comment: Landscape plan must identify all trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors and 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors, verify that species match ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated trees with mature height ≤20 feet), and include note requiring property owner responsibility for ongoing tree pruning/removal within 10 feet of centerline of overhead electric facilities per Austin Energy standard practice and Block 8 requirements.
applicableAreas: Tree plantings on landscape plan, particularly within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors
observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan, guide.md) explicitly states: 'Block 2: drawing — Main Landscape and Site Plan. A comprehensive site plan illustrating building footprints, parking layouts, sidewalks, utility lines (Water, Storm Drain, Overhead Electric), topographical contours, and the distribution of landscape elements.' This confirms overhead electric lines are shown on the landscape plan. The sheet index shows Sheets 30-35, 37 address trees and landscaping. However, NO dimension annotations or notes on the landscape plan specify which species are planted within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors, and no reference is made to ECM Appendix F Utility Compatible Shade Trees list ('UC'-designated species). Without specific callouts showing tree locations relative to overhead conductors and without verification of species against the UC list, compliance cannot be confirmed. Trees exceeding the utility-compatible size/species may be planted in violation of clearance and future maintenance conflicts with the electric utility.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies a 50-lateral-foot clearance requirement for trees near transmission lines (more restrictive than the 30-40 feet mentioned in ECM § 2.4.1.D/2.4.2.C). Trees within these clearance zones must be from the Utility Compatible list (ECM Appendix F, marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). The landscape plan shows tree plantings and site grading but provides NO verification that trees within 10 feet of distribution or 50 feet of transmission conductors are utility-compatible species. Additionally, Sheet 3, Block 8 requires that 'owner shall be responsible for any initial tree pruning and tree removal that is within ten feet of the center line of the proposed overhead electric facilities.' This suggests applicant acknowledges trees are a concern, but the landscape plan does not address compatibility.

comment: Clearly depict on site plan the location of existing down guy wire anchor points shown on the existing survey (Sheet 4). Verify that proposed driveways, accessible paths, parking areas, and other site features do not conflict with guy anchors or guy wire cables. If conflicts exist, provide notes addressing resolution through pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting steel poles per utility company standards.
applicableAreas: Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features relative to down guy wires from existing utility poles
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a 'GUY ANCHOR' symbol (per the legend) at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road, indicating down guy wires are present on the existing utility infrastructure. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site layout with driveways, sidewalks, and pedestrian paths, but does NOT depict existing guy wire locations or down guy anchor points. The survey shows the guy anchor exists, but its location relative to the proposed driveways and accessible paths is not dimensioned or verified on Sheet 9. Without down guy wire locations being shown on the site plan and without verification that proposed accessible routes, driveways, or site features do not conflict with guy anchors and cables, compliance cannot be confirmed.
reasoning: Down guy wires are support cables from distribution utility poles to ground anchors. They represent a potential obstruction and conflict risk if proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features are routed over or through the guy anchor zone. UCM § 1.17.0 (Glossary) defines 'Down Guy' as a distinct feature. The grouping guidance notes that electric utility infrastructure (poles, guy wires, guys) is 'frequently omitted from plans,' suggesting this is a common deficiency. Sheet 4 confirms a guy anchor exists, but Sheet 9 does not show where it is located in relation to proposed site features. If the guy anchor conflicts with proposed improvements, the code requires either (1) pole relocation, or (2) conversion to self-supporting steel poles. The applicant has not addressed this possibility.

comment: Depict on site plan and plat all down guy anchor easement boundaries for existing utility poles, showing 10-foot easement width extending minimum 5 feet past the point where the guy wire enters the ground. Verify that proposed site features (buildings, driveways, sidewalks, landscaping) do not encroach on or obstruct the down guy anchor easement area.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from existing utility poles
observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows a guy anchor symbol at one of the utility poles along Valley View Road. Sheet 2 (Plat) should show easement boundaries, but facts.md indicates that critical easements are not depicted on the submitted site plan. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not show or reference down guy anchor easement boundaries. The grouping guidance specifies that down guy anchor easement requirements are: '10 feet wide extending 5 feet past where down guy enters ground' (per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards). Without easement boundaries shown on the plat or site plan, and without dimension annotations confirming the 10-foot width and 5-foot extension, compliance cannot be verified.
reasoning: According to Reviewer Convention and Austin Energy standards, down guy anchor points require dedicated easements to ensure access for maintenance, replacement, and inspection. The required easement is 10 feet wide with minimum 5-foot extension beyond the anchor ground entry point. The existing survey (Sheet 4) confirms a guy anchor exists, but the plat (Sheet 2) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not show or reference the dedicated easement for this anchor. Without easement boundaries shown and dimensioned, applicant has not demonstrated that required easement space is provided and protected from development impacts (buildings, paving, landscaping, etc.).

comment: Provide section views of proposed transformer pads showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum 7.5-foot vertical clearance from the lowest point of overhead conductors to the highest point of transformer equipment. If transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines, provide specific clearance verification or relocation notes.
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows multiple transformer pad locations throughout the site (labeled 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' at several locations). However, the electrical plan is a plan view showing horizontal placement only. NO section views or elevation drawings accompany the electrical plan showing the vertical relationship between transformer pad height and the surveyed elevation of overhead electric conductors above the site. No vertical clearance dimension annotations are present. Overhead electric lines are shown on the plan as existing 'OHE' lines on the western and southern boundaries, but no section showing the clearance from these conductors to the tops of transformer pads is provided.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires transformers (whether pole-mounted or pad-mounted) to maintain minimum 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance from overhead electric lines. This is a vertical clearance requirement, requiring knowledge of both the transformer height and the conductor height. The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations but does not provide the surveyed conductor elevation or section views demonstrating that the 7.5-foot clearance is maintained. This is particularly important if any transformers are located beneath existing overhead lines or where overhead conductors pass over transformer equipment.

comment: Provide construction staging/logistics plan (or site phasing plan) showing: (1) all proposed equipment staging areas, material storage zones, and laydown areas; (2) 10-foot radial clearance boundaries from overhead distribution lines (marked as exclusion zones); (3) crane swing radius zones with 10-foot radial clearance from energized lines; (4) 20-foot clearance from transmission lines if transmission structures are present; (5) note requiring contractor to maintain clearances and reference to OSHA 1910.333 working clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, material storage zones, and equipment laydown areas throughout the site
observation: Sheet 5 (Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan) addresses temporary erosion control measures and construction sequencing but does not include a detailed construction staging plan or equipment layout plan showing staging areas, equipment zones, crane swing radius, or material storage locations in relation to overhead electric lines. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the general site development layout but does not designate specific construction staging areas or address 10-foot radial clearances during construction. NO plans address OSHA and UCM § 1.10.2 requirements for 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines during construction activities. The sheet list shows no separate 'Construction Phasing Plan' or 'Construction Staging Plan' sheet.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 references OSHA 1910.333 and Texas law requirements for construction working clearances. The grouping guidance states: 'Minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) [for] construction working clearances.' This is a mandatory safety requirement during construction and is distinct from permanent clearances. Additionally, the grouping notes: 'OSHA requires a 20-foot clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' The plans do not demonstrate that construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms will maintain required clearances from overhead energized lines. This is a deficiency: applicant has failed to provide a construction staging/logistics plan addressing these safety clearances.

comment: Add note to cover sheet (Sheet 1) or general notes (Sheet 3) stating: 'Owner and contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before beginning any work, excavation, or construction activities within or adjacent to areas containing overhead electric facilities and lines. Notification is required by Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, and UCM § 1.10.2. Contact information: [Austin Energy contact details]. Failure to notify may result in serious injury, fatality, or project delays.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet and general notes for entire project
observation: Comprehensive review of Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) and Sheet 3 (General Notes) reveals the following: Sheet 1 contains project title, location map, fire department requirements, environmental notes, various compliance statements, but NO note requiring 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work begins near overhead lines. Sheet 3, Block 20 includes 'Electric Transmission Notes' (16 items) which specifically require (Item 3): 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction... OSHA requires a 20' clearance from energized transmission lines during construction.' This note applies specifically to TRANSMISSION facilities and includes a 48-hour requirement for a SAFETY MEETING. However, Sheet 3, Blocks 8/14 ('Electric Notes') address general distribution lines but contain NO requirement for 48-hour notification before construction work begins near distribution overhead lines. Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003, requires notification to utilities before work on high-voltage lines, and UCM § 1.10.2 incorporates this requirement. The plans do not include this general notification requirement for distribution lines.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 explicitly requires a plan note: 'Plans must include note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines (Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003).' While Sheet 3, Block 20 requires a 48-hour pre-construction safety MEETING for transmission lines specifically, there is NO corresponding note for general construction notification before work begins near distribution overhead lines. This is a regulatory and safety requirement distinct from the transmission-specific safety meeting. The note is required to be on the cover sheet or in the general notes to inform owner, contractor, and City of the notification requirement.

comment: Plant schedule lists tree species proposed near overhead electric line, but does not document utility-compatible (UC) status per ECM Appendix F required by UCM § 1.10.10.4. Clearance distances from tree trunks to outside conductors are not dimensioned on landscape plan, preventing verification of compliance with 15-foot minimum distance for non-utility-compatible species near distribution conductors.
applicableAreas: western site boundary where overhead electric line is present
areas within 15 feet of overhead distribution conductor
observation: Sheet 21 documents an existing overhead electric line (OHE) running along the western boundary with utility poles and a service transition to underground infrastructure. Sheet 31 (landscape plan) shows the OHE line and depicts trees positioned along the site boundary near this overhead line. observation: Sheet 21 shows electric facilities labeled with generic text callouts: 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters', and 'Underground Electric Line'. While these labels ARE legible and visible, they provide NO technical identification of the facilities. Labels do not indicate: (1) type with any specificity, (2) voltage level, (3) capacity/size, (4) ownership (AE vs. Customer), (5) whether underground or overhead, or (6) material specifications. Sheet 9 similarly shows only generic 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and 'OHE' labels without detail. The labels fail to provide the level of identification necessary for clear plan review and code compliance verification.
reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that electric facilities be 'clearly labeled' with identification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Generic "existing utility" notation without specifying electric facility type, voltage, size, ownership' is identified as a common violation pattern. The applicant has used generic type-only labels without the required technical specifications. This deficiency prevents Austin Energy and City reviewers from clearly understanding what facilities are shown and their code compliance status.

The grouping regulatory overview lists 'Labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information' as a common violation pattern. comment: Electric notes are duplicated on the same sheet. Please remove the duplicate electric notes from Sheet 3 and retain only one complete set of consolidated electric notes on the general notes sheet.

observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains the 'Electric Notes' block showing 5 numbered notes addressing Austin Energy requirements (notes 1-5). reasoning: Reviewer Convention established in the grouping requires that 'Electric notes [should be] consolidated on cover sheet or general notes sheet' (singular instance), not duplicated. The applicant has consolidated the notes to the general notes sheet, which is correct, but then unnecessarily repeated them within the same block, which creates confusion and increases visual clutter without providing additional information. Best practice requires notes to appear once in a consolidated location.

comment: Electric utility easements are not clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans. Please add clear visual delineation (shading, hatch pattern, or bold boundary lines) to distinguish electric utility easements from the surrounding site area on site plan and utility plan, with labels showing easement width and recorded instrument numbers.
applicableAreas: Site plan and utility plan; all property boundaries
observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show utility easements with text labels: '5' P.U.E.', '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', '3' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', and others. However, these easements are shown using only text labels and line work similar to other utility lines. They are NOT clearly delineated with visual emphasis (no distinct shading, hatch pattern, bold lines, or graphic distinction) that would make them stand out for clear identification and review. The grouping guidance states that this is an 'All sites' applicable requirement. Clear delineation means visual distinction that allows reviewers to readily identify and understand easement boundaries. Text labels alone without visual emphasis are insufficient. The applicant must use graphic techniques (color fill, hatch pattern, bold boundary lines, or other standard plan representation) to clearly distinguish easement areas from surrounding site area.

comment: Projected load for electric service is not provided on electrical plans. Please provide the calculated electrical load for the proposed development (in kVA or kW) based on the 39 residential townhome units and any common area electrical requirements, and submit for Austin Energy capacity verification.
observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 3 (General Notes), and facts.md project summary. No electrical load information is shown on any sheet. reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that 'Projected load [be] required for electric service' for projects with new or upgraded electric service. This project is clearly a new development with 39 units requiring new electric service. The applicant must provide electrical load calculations showing the total demand (in kVA or kW) for the project based on the 39-unit residential load and any common area requirements. This information is required by Austin Energy for service adequacy verification and is fundamental to the preliminary electrical design.

comment: Provide dimensioned clearances from all four transformer pads to adjacent buildings, parking areas, driveways, and structures per UCM § 1.10.4 requirements (10 feet for hot-stick use area, 5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3-5 feet for other sides depending on building construction type). Confirm building construction types if any clearances are less than standard requirements.
applicableAreas: Four transformer pad locations on the site
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies four locations labeled "Electrical Transformer Pad": (1) west of Building 1 near Unit 101, (2) west of Building 8 near Unit 801, (3) south of Building 5 near Unit 504, and (4) north of Building 7 near Unit 705. All four pads are shown as simple squares with no dimension lines showing clearances to adjacent buildings, parking areas, walkways, or structures. The site plan shows driveways and parking areas in close proximity to these pads, but no distances are dimensioned.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 specifies clearance requirements for pad-mounted equipment based on the type of adjacent structures and whether the equipment has operator/control access. Required clearances range from 3 feet (non-operator sides, non-brick/masonry buildings) to 10 feet (hot-stick use area). The absence of dimensioned clearances prevents verification that the design complies with these minimum setbacks and prevents determination of whether reduced clearances (3 feet instead of 5 feet) require AE Design written approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Building construction type (brick/masonry with 2-hour fire rating vs. non-brick/masonry) must be documented to determine which clearance column in Table 1.10.4 applies.

comment: Add transmission notes to Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) referencing the detailed transmission clearance and access requirements shown on the general notes sheet, or verify that transmission facilities do not exist and remove transmission notes from Sheet 3 if inapplicable.
applicableAreas: Transmission easement area (if transmission facilities present on site)
observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains an extensive "Electric Transmission Notes" section with 16 numbered items covering transmission clearances, digging restrictions, access requirements, and construction safety. However, examination of Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no transmission-related notes—only standard utility easement references and general drainage/construction notes. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) likewise contains no transmission-related notes; the blocks shown reference only irrigation notes, general landscape notes, and legend definitions, with no text addressing transmission facilities, clearance zones, or construction restrictions related to transmission.

The presence of comprehensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggests transmission facilities exist on or immediately adjacent to the site. Transmission facilities have substantially different access and construction restrictions than distribution facilities and require special contractor awareness and coordination with Austin Energy (per the 16 transmission notes on Sheet 3, including 48-hour pre-construction safety meeting, 25-foot clearance from structures, OSHA 20-foot clearance from energized lines, etc.). Contractors and workers reviewing the grading plan or landscape plan would have no awareness of these transmission-specific constraints, which creates a safety and compliance risk.

comment: Transformer pads shown on electrical design plan lack documented clearance measurements to adjacent buildings. Provide dimensioned drawings or calculations demonstrating minimum 5-foot clearance from edge of transformer pad to building foundations and exterior walls.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 west side near Building 2
Transformer Pad 2 west side near Building 8
observation: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows three transformer pads as dotted rectangles. Pads 1 and 2 are positioned on the west side of the site near Buildings 2 and 8 respectively, in proximity to the property line and sidewalk easement areas. Site plan (Sheet 9) shows general building layout but does not include dimensional clearance measurements between the transformer pads and building facades. Vision analysis confirms Pad 1 is positioned between Building 2 and the western property boundary (sidewalk area), and Pad 2 is positioned similarly near Building 8. However, no numerical measurements (e.g., "5 feet minimum") are provided on any submitted plan sheets to document actual clearances from building foundations or structures.
reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 requires a minimum 5-foot clearance from pad-mounted equipment to buildings, structures, and building foundations. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating compliance through documented measurements or calculations on the plans. While the plans show transformer pad locations and building positions, the absence of explicit clearance measurements between the pad edges and building walls prevents verification of compliance. This constitutes failure to document the required clearances, not merely unclear positioning. However, since the pads are shown at some distance from the buildings (not touching), the deficiency cannot be definitively proven as a pass or fail without actual measurements. This requires clarification through submission of dimensional drawings showing clearances.

comment: Transformer Pads 1 and 2 shown near sidewalk easements on electrical plan lack documented clearance measurements. Provide dimensioned drawings demonstrating minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to edge of transformer pad.

Site plan (Sheet 9) shows sidewalk/pedestrian areas along Valley View Road. Grading plan (Sheet 11) indicates curb elevations and pedestrian access areas. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirms sidewalk easement marking near both western pads. However, no explicit measurements are provided documenting the distance from the back of the sidewalk to the transformer pad edges.

Sidewalk easements are clearly depicted on the electrical plan in proximity to Pads 1 and 2, but without dimensional documentation (measurements in feet) on the plans, the actual clearance cannot be verified. The pads appear to be positioned nearby the sidewalk area, but confirmation of the specific 2-foot minimum requires dimensioned drawings.

comment: Transformer pad access door orientation not indicated on electrical design plan. Provide documentation showing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door and demonstrating minimum 10-foot clearance from the access door side to open area or adjacent structure.

Without knowing which side of each transformer pad contains the access door, it is impossible to verify whether the required 10-foot clearance exists in the appropriate direction. The plans must indicate access door orientation and the associated 10-foot use area to demonstrate compliance.

comment: Transformer Pad 3 located between multiple buildings in central courtyard area. Provide documentation clarifying whether the pad access door faces a confined space (3+ sides enclosed). If confined space applies, provide dimensioned drawings or cross-sections demonstrating minimum 15-foot clearance from access door.
applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 3 central location between Buildings 4, 5, and 6

Transformer Pad 3's location between three buildings suggests it may face a confined space orientation on one or more sides. However, without access door orientation documentation and no cross-section drawings demonstrating the configuration, it cannot be determined whether the 15-foot confined space threshold applies or whether the applicable clearance requirement has been met.

comment: Landscape plan does not show root barrier details or specifications for trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations. Provide landscape detail drawings showing root barrier locations, dimensions (minimum 4 feet deep), installation setbacks (5 feet from transformer equipment), and materials for all trees within 20 feet of transformer pads.
applicableAreas: All proposed landscape trees within 20 lateral feet of transformer pad locations
observation: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) and landscape details sheet (Sheet 37) reviewed for root barrier specifications. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 confirms that trees are shown throughout the site perimeter with various designations (M, SY, PL, P), but the plan notes and key notes do not include any reference to root barriers, root barrier details, or specifications for trees in proximity to utilities. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) would typically contain root barrier detail specifications but was not examined in detail. comment: Sheet 21 references an 'Electrical Vault Easement' but the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' Clarify whether the transformer is pad-mounted (compliant) or installed in a subsurface vault (non-compliant outside Network Area per UCM § 1.5.2.6). If a vault installation is proposed outside the Network Area, reconfigure to either: (a) pad-mounted transformer (clear to sky), or (b) specialized niche meeting UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3 requirements (35-foot vertical clearance, 3-hour fire-rated walls/ceilings, exterior access, proper ventilation, truck accessibility).
observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) visual analysis identified the presence of an 'Electrical Vault Easement' labeled near the southwest entrance of the site. The vision analysis noted this easement 'encompasses a transformer pad and pull box.' The site is located at 3759 Valley View Road, Austin TX 78704 in the MF-2 zoning district, which is not part of the downtown Network Area (UCM § 1.11.5). No Network Area service is indicated on the site plans. The term 'vault easement' is used in the labeling, but the transformer within it is described as a 'pad' (pad-mounted), which typically refers to aboveground equipment. However, the use of the term 'vault' in the easement designation creates ambiguity as to whether the transformer is truly a subsurface vault installation or simply an easement area serving a pad-mounted transformer.
reasoning: EL-19.22 specifies 'Vaults or meter rooms proposed outside Network Area where vaults are not permitted' and applies only when 'vaults or subsurface/enclosed transformer rooms are proposed.' UCM § 1.5.2.6 restricts transformer vaults to the Network Area only; outside the Network Area, transformers must be pad-mounted (clear to sky) or installed in specialized niches meeting specific requirements (UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 3). The site is clearly outside the Network Area. The ambiguity arises from the sheet's reference to an 'Electrical Vault Easement' while the transformer within it is labeled as a 'pad.' This terminology conflict must be clarified: if the transformer is truly installed in a subsurface vault, it violates UCM § 1.5.2.6. If it is a pad-mounted transformer within an easement area, it is compliant. The preliminary nature of the electrical plan and lack of detailed transformer installation specifications (normal pad-mounted vs. vault vs. niche configuration) prevent a definitive determination.
